transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-26 | Start: 14:00 UTC | Duration: ~57 minutes
Attendees: Marcus Green (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Alex Romero (DeepCache Head of ML), Dana Liu (CTO), Samir Patel (Platform Eng)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
DeepCache Logistics is evaluating Redwood for a mix of hosted and private deployments. Primary needs: long context (60k+ token threads for parcel tracking + manifests), multilingual support (EN, ES, PT), and robust tool-calling for internal microservices (inventory lookup, route optimization). They are sensitive to PII/data residency and want SOC2 docs and a pilot on their k8s infra. Discussion covered open model tradeoffs (Mistral, Llama derivatives, local quantized variants), batching/latency tradeoffs, KV/prefix caching, and dedicated vs private (VPC) options. Next steps: pricing breakdown, security pack, pilot plan, benchmark session.

Topics covered: open model comparison; context length and memory footprint; multilingual quality; function/tool-calling reliability; hosted vs Dedicated vs Private; compliance (SOC2, SSO, KMS); pilot and benchmarks.

Action items (auto):
- Marcus: send pricing breakouts + pilot contract draft

- Samir: infra constraints and access for pilot

Transcript body:
[00:00] Marcus: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Marcus from Redwood, AE. We've got Priya, our solutions engineer, on too. How are you all?
[00:07] Dana: Good, thanks. Busy but good.
[00:09] Alex: Hey, thanks for making time. We wanted to run through what we need and see where Redwood fits.
[00:14] Marcus: Great. Can you give us a quick overview of the use cases and must-haves?
[00:18] Alex: Sure. At a high level: parcel tracking, manifests ingestion, and a customer support assistant that needs full shipment history. The kicker is we want very long context — think 40k to 70k tokens per conversation sometimes, because manifests plus event streams need to be in context. Also multilingual — EN, Spanish, Portuguese — and we need to call internal services: inventory lookup, ETA service, pricing, so tool-calling is a hard requirement.
[00:40] Priya: Got it. When you say tool-calling, do you mean function-calling style sync calls, or async webhooks, or both?
[00:45] Samir: Mostly sync RPC-style calls — we have microservices behind an internal API. We want the model to decide which calls to invoke and pass structured args.
[00:52] Marcus: That's supported — we've got function-calling and structured output. There are some nuances between models in how deterministic they are for tool selection, and also runtime implications depending on batching and latency.
[01:05] Alex: Yeah, that's one of our concerns. We need a throughput target of ~150 requests per second for core APIs during peak, and tail latency sub-300ms for short lookups. For the long context agents, higher latency is acceptable.
[01:20] Priya: This is where Dedicated pools can help. You can reserve GPU capacity to get predictable tail latency. Hosted can be cheaper to start with, but you'd see more variance during bursts. For 150 RPS with long context, we typically suggest a mixed approach: Hosted for low-latency, short-context endpoints and Dedicated for heavy long-context workloads.
[01:38] Dana: What about privacy? We can't send manifests with PII to a shared model unless it's encrypted or we have clear data retention policies.
[01:45] Marcus: Understood. For Private deployments we can run a customer-managed control plane in your VPC or on-prem. We support KMS integrations for key management and can offer an on-prem package if you need air-gapped. For Hosted, we have options for data retention and redaction, but it's not the same as private.
[02:03] Samir: Do you have SOC2 and ISO certs? We need that for procurement.
[02:07] Marcus: Yes, we have SOC2 Type II. I'll share the compliance pack after the call.
[02:12] Alex: Great. Let's talk models. We tried a few open models internally — Mistral variants, Llama 3 style, and some quantized 8-bit variants. We saw big quality drops in Spanish and Portuguese on some quantized variants.
[02:26] Priya: That matches what we've seen. For multilingual, model family matters — some larger Mistral and Llama-derivatives maintain multilingual quality even when quantized to INT8, but smaller quantized models sometimes alternate weirdly on tokenization at language boundaries. Also, context length support differs: some community forks support 64k, some up to 128k with custom attention kernels.
[02:45] Alex: We heard Redwood has a profile of verified performance across models — can you help pick candidates?
[02:50] Marcus: Yes, we have a model catalog with performance profiles and suggestions. For long context multilingual + tool-calling, a common choice is a 64k-capable Mistral-large or a tuned Llama-derivative with optimized KV cache. For us it's also about runtime: continuous KV caching and prefix caching can reduce tokens sent to the model and save cost/latency.
[03:10] Dana: How reliable is function-calling across model switchover? If we do rollouts, will the call signatures break?
[03:17] Priya: We tackle that with output schemas and canaries. Redwood's rollouts let you map identical function schemas across variants and fallback automatically. There can be small differences in generation; we recommend a schema validation layer and canary traffic to a new model for a few thousand calls to surface regressions.
[03:33] Alex: Any quirks with KV cache? Our workloads have long-running sessions; we aim to reuse history without resending full messages every time.
[03:40] Priya: KV cache is exactly for that. In Dedicated/private you can persist the KV cache per session and only send deltas. We also offer prefix caching for common templates. Note: some models' KVM formats aren't compatible across families, so you need to keep cache compatibility in mind when switching model backbone.
[03:58] Samir: From infra side — our k8s cluster runs A100s and a couple of H100s for bursts. What's the recommended quant/precision and memory profile?
[04:07] Priya: A100s are great for int8 quantized inference. H100s give better throughput on fp16/4-bit kernels. For 64k context, memory becomes a limiter; we usually recommend either chained attention kernels or models compiled with efficient attention. There are tradeoffs: lower precision saves memory but can impact multilingual fidelity.
[04:28] Alex: Let's talk numbers. Any back-of-envelope for cost delta between hosted and dedicated for 64k runs?
[04:35] Marcus: Very rough: Hosted per-token cost will be higher and more spiky. Dedicated amortizes GPU cost — for sustained heavy usage it's often 30-60% cheaper per token depending on utilization and batching. But initial commitment and reserved capacity fees apply. We'll send a more detailed breakout.
[04:52] Dana: What about scaling? If we need burst to 300 RPS for a flash sale, can Dedicated burst into Hosted or other regions?
[04:59] Priya: Yes, Redwood supports smart routing and automated fallback. You can route by policy — primary to Dedicated, fallback to Hosted or other compatible model variants. There's configuration for cost vs latency.
[05:10] Alex: We have an internal rule: no customer PII leaves our VPC. That pushes us toward Private. But we'd prefer to pilot Hosted to move fast. Any hybrid patterns?
[05:20] Marcus: Hybrid is common: keep PII-sensitive operations in Private/Dedicated and offload anonymized, lower-sensitivity queries to Hosted for scale. We can also run inference in your VPC with a Redwood Dedicated control plane so you get management while data stays in your network.
[05:34] Dana: For the pilot, what would you need?
[05:37] Priya: Ideally: (1) a sample prompt set, including manifests and multi-turn examples, (2) a small dataset for multilingual evaluation, (3) API access to your test microservices for tool-calling, (4) infra details — pod sizes, GPU types, egress limits. We'll run a two-week pilot with a reproducible benchmark harness.
[05:56] Samir: We can provide a sandbox cluster with limited access and tokens.
[05:59] Alex: Good. Also — latency SLOs: for the support assistant we can tolerate 800-1,200ms; for inventory lookups we need <300ms.
[06:10] Priya: We'll design two profiles: a short-context low-latency route and a long-context archival route. The short route benefits from batching and lower context models. The long-context route uses dedicated GPUs and KV persistence.
[06:22] Marcus: Quick note on model hygiene — we recommend evaluation harnesses and regression alerts tied to your prompt sets. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization and model switching thresholds if quality dips.
[06:33] Alex: Any gotchas with multilingual tokenizers? We had tokenization drift after quantization where Portuguese got weird segmentation and hallucinated addresses.
[06:41] Priya: That can happen. We run language-specific eval sets and will test quantized variants side-by-side with fp16 baselines. If segmentation is an issue, sometimes a slightly larger model at lower quant gives better tradeoff.
[06:55] Dana: Security: SSO, RBAC, audit logs — does Redwood integrate with our SAML provider and central logging?
[07:02] Marcus: Yep — SSO via SAML/Okta supported, RBAC on the console, and audit logs shipped to your SIEM. For Private you can keep logs on-prem. We'll attach the integration doc.
[07:14] Alex: Competitor question — we talked to Anthropic and some boutique providers. Why Redwood?
[07:19] Marcus: Two things: production-first developer experience and unified inference across environments. We focus on predictable latency and tools for deployment — rollouts, tracing, and cost controls. We also have a model catalog with verified performance, which speeds iterations.
[07:32] Samir: Could we see a sample benchmark?
[07:35] Priya: Yes — I'll prep a benchmark plan and a sample spreadsheet. We'll include token-level latency, cost, and multilingual accuracy.
[07:43] Alex: Great. Any immediate blockers?
[07:46] Dana: Procurement will need SOC2 and a network diagram.
[07:49] Marcus: I'll send SOC2, some network architecture examples, and a starter contract.
[07:54] Alex: Excellent. Let's recap next steps.
[07:57] Marcus: Recap: 1) Marcus to send Hosted vs Dedicated pricing and compliance pack; 2) Priya will prepare benchmark plan + prompt set and run the initial tests; 3) Samir to share infra constraints and provide sandbox access; 4) Schedule on-site benchmark week of Sep 6 if that works.
[08:20] Dana: Sep 6 week looks doable.
[08:22] Alex: Thanks everyone. That was helpful.
[08:25] Marcus: Thanks — we'll follow up with the docs and scheduling invites.
[08:28] (call ends)

Notes about transcription: occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "KV cache" transcribed as "K-V cash") and proper nouns may be imperfect. There were a few cross-talk moments where speaker attribution is fuzzy.
